clue.text: The speed, by the way, is not excessive

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece sits next to the other

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
a rate is a speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Someone reassures us that the speed on this road is perfectly reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moderate is kept within reasonable limits, avoiding extremes.

clue.text: Part of body represented by one in parliament

definitions.meaning: a limb such as an arm or leg
an elected MP sits for a constituency

explanation.surface: A body part stands for someone sitting in parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is called a member, and so is an elected representative such as an MP.

clue.text: Made baby's bed in Berkshire

parts.note: did is a past tense of do, as in made or performed
a cot is a small bed with sides for an infant

explanation.surface: Someone assembled a crib for an infant somewhere in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: DIDCOT is a railway town that lay in the English county of Berkshire when this was set; boundary changes in 1974 moved it into Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The town was historically part of the county of Berkshire, west of London.

clue.text: First steam train to orbit the earth

definitions.text: First steam train to orbit the earth

parts.words: First steam train to orbit the earth
parts.note: reads as a locomotive in space, but joins Stephenson's pioneering 1829 engine with the vehicle that launches satellites

explanation.surface: An absurd image of a pioneering steam locomotive circling the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephenson's famous early locomotive bore this name, which is also a launch vehicle for space flight.

clue.text: Sports club dance hard hit when its members rally

definitions.meaning: a formal dance held by a racket club

definitions.text: hard hit when its members rally
definitions.meaning: the yellow ball struck back and forth in rallies on court

explanation.surface: At a sports club dance, members gather and hit things hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance put on by a racket club, and the ball struck in rallies by its players.

clue.text: What famine victims may do despite vaster redistribution

indicators.note: the letters of vaster are shared out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Even though wealth is spread more widely, famine victims still go hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: People in a famine go without food and may die of hunger.

clue.text: He is in a depression, as any golfer would be who lands in it

definitions.text: as any golfer would be who lands in it

indicators.note: says the word he sits inside the following depression

parts.note: a trough is a low point or hollow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is feeling low, like a golfer who has hit his ball into a hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' is the container signal. 'Depression' doubles in the surface as low spirits, while the definition means the long grass beside a golf fairway, where a wayward shot ends up.
explanation.definitionFit: The long grass off the fairway is where a stray golf shot ends up.

clue.text: Jolly fine music made by castanets

definitions.meaning: very good, as in a dated phrase for a cracking good story
the clicking clatter of the instruments

explanation.surface: Castanets make very fine music.
explanation.definitionFit: The old intensifier means very or excellent, and the word also names the clattering noise castanets give.

clue.text: Hartnell fashion revealing trans-Atlantic charm

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters of Hartnell are reshaped

explanation.surface: Designs by couturier Norman Hartnell show American charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Hartnell was a British couturier, the Queen's dressmaker, so 'fashion' looks like part of the surface. 'trans-Atlantic' marks the American spelling with a double L.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate or charm someone; the doubled L is the American spelling.

clue.text: Specific Florentine family born in France

parts.note: the Medici were the ruling banking dynasty of Florence
né is French for born

explanation.surface: A particular Florentine dynasty had French origins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Specific' looks like an adjective, but as a noun it means a remedy for a particular ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific is a remedy aimed at one particular disease.

clue.text: Get going fast it's the only way to break a record

definitions.text: the only way to break a record
definitions.meaning: you must surpass the existing best

explanation.surface: Advice that a record can only be broken by surpassing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for go away, and also what you must do to the existing best to break a record.

clue.text: Coteries contrive to be confidential

indicators.note: to contrive is to devise, so the letters of coteries are devised anew

explanation.surface: Cliques scheme to keep their matters secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge understood only by a small inner circle is secret or private.

clue.text: Refrigerator jug

definitions.meaning: an appliance or box that chills things

explanation.surface: A fridge and a pitcher, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilling box or appliance, and slang for prison, like jug or clink.

clue.text: Give-aways for those who do 25 across

definitions.text: Give-aways for those who do 25 across

parts.words: Give-aways for those who do 25 across
parts.note: reading the cross-referenced answer as an instruction to reward hotel workers, these are the sums handed over

explanation.surface: Presents for people who carry out another answer's advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tips are small sums freely given to service workers.

clue.text: Able-bodied and ingenious native

parts.note: AB stands for able-bodied seaman
original means inventive or creative

explanation.surface: A local inhabitant who is fit and clever.
explanation.definitionFit: An indigenous inhabitant of a land, there from earliest times.

clue.text: A tiny piece but a great deal more than one can take

parts.note: a bit is a small fragment
much means a large amount

explanation.surface: A paradox: a tiny piece is nevertheless far too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, something excessive or unreasonable to put up with.

clue.text: Something wrong with the hi fi? Then ask someone for his opinion

definitions.text: Something wrong with the hi fi?
definitions.meaning: the stereo has gone silent, its audio having failed
to probe a person's views discreetly

explanation.surface: When the stereo is broken, consult someone about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass a person's views; read literally, the audio has stopped.

clue.text: He's in a disreputable club, and with it he can stick

indicators.note: places the letters of he's inside the club

parts.note: a dive is a seedy nightclub or bar
the contraction taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A man in a seedy club who is with it can stay the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue or similar sticky material is what lets something stick.

clue.text: The most appropriate fabric for a Norfolk boating jacket?

definitions.text: The most appropriate fabric for a Norfolk boating jacket?

parts.words: The most appropriate fabric for a Norfolk boating jacket?
parts.note: the Norfolk Broads are waterways in eastern England popular for boating, so a cloth named after them would suit

explanation.surface: Which material best suits a jacket for sailing in Norfolk?
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England, a popular boating holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine dense woollen or cotton fabric used for suits and shirts.

clue.text: Tenant casually voices a request to view

indicators.note: spoken in a slurred everyday way, the phrase sounds like the entry

parts.note: let's see is how you ask to look at something

explanation.surface: A tenant offhandedly asks to look round.
explanation.definitionFit: One who holds property on a lease is a renter.

clue.text: Drains changed for change's sake in Yugoslavia

indicators.note: the letters of drains are altered in order

explanation.surface: Plumbing was altered just for the sake of it in Yugoslavia.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as what you would use for loose change in Yugoslavia, whose currency unit this was.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency unit of the former Yugoslavia, so coins used as change there.

clue.text: He sets fire a little lower

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: sets means arranges, so the letters of fire are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A man lights a fire a bit further down.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lower' here is something that lows, i.e. moos, not something further down.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cow is a small animal that moos.

clue.text: He treats skin and hides a silver sixpence

definitions.meaning: a worker who cures leather from animal pelts
old British slang for a sixpenny coin

explanation.surface: A leather-worker conceals a small coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Before decimalisation in 1971 a sixpence (half a shilling) was a small British coin, nicknamed with this word.
explanation.definitionFit: One who cures animal pelts into leather; also old slang for the sixpenny coin.

clue.text: Fellow likely to shock more sedate types?

definitions.text: Fellow likely to shock more sedate types?

parts.words: Fellow likely to shock more sedate types?
parts.note: a lively energetic person, pictured as an electrified cable that would jolt anyone touching it

explanation.surface: A man whose behaviour scandalises staid people.
explanation.definitionFit: An energetic vibrant person, likened to a cable carrying current.

clue.text: Land of Good Hope represented in Bantu topiary

indicators.note: the letters are shown inside the run of these two words

explanation.surface: An ideal land depicted in African hedge-clipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good Hope' suggests the Cape of Good Hope, fitting the Bantu surface, but the definition is an imagined perfect land.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's ideal commonwealth, a land of perfect hopes.

clue.text: Court official advising hotel guests to show generosity

definitions.meaning: an usher or bailiff in a court of law

definitions.text: advising hotel guests to show generosity
definitions.meaning: telling guests to give gratuities to employees

explanation.surface: A court officer suggests guests reward the hotel workers.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer of a law court carrying a staff; read as two words, an instruction to reward employees.

clue.text: Den of iniquity in which retiring types shouldn't get cold feet

definitions.text: in which retiring types shouldn't get cold feet
definitions.meaning: a warm bed for those going to sleep

explanation.surface: A disreputable den where people going to bed should stay warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' here means going to bed, not shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeding ground for vice; literally a warmed bed.

clue.text: One who values ancient coins of copper with head of solid gold

parts.note: the as was a Roman copper coin, plural asses

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of solid

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A valuer examines old copper coins with a pure gold top.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuer or appraiser estimates worth, for tax or insurance.
